subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose general private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the supported shape be a global dangerous flag, per-agent SSRF policy, or narrower hostname-scoped exceptions?
rationale: The lower-level guard can allow private networks, but exposing it through `web_fetch` changes a security boundary and public config surface; automation cannot choose the acceptable operator trust model or metadata/redirect policy.

options.title: Prefer per-agent SSRF policy
options.body: Continue from the maintainer draft direction so private-network access can be restricted to named trusted agents and surfaced in audit output.

options.title: Accept a global dangerous flag
options.body: Expose a global `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork` knob with strong docs and tests, accepting broader operator blast radius.

options.title: Decline broad opt-in for now
options.body: Keep arbitrary `web_fetch` strict and steer users toward trusted proxies, provider-specific exact-origin trust, or future allowlist/confirmation work.

recommendation.title: Prefer per-agent SSRF policy
recommendation.body: Continue from the maintainer draft direction so private-network access can be restricted to named trusted agents and surfaced in audit output.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the narrower SSRF policy fix and explicitly identified this issue as a separate security-sensitive config decision.
